senses.definition: Directly and without hedging, usually about where something belongs or who owns it.
senses.caution: Use it about who owns something or which group it belongs in. If the point is still disputed, it overclaims and invites people to push back.
senses.example: Cost governance sits squarely with the platform team, not with each product.

cues.text: A director asks who owns model evaluation. It is the platform team, and you want to say so in a way that ends the question.
Legal asks whether the new regulation covers your product. It does, entirely, and you want one adverb that removes the wiggle room.
You are writing a post-incident memo and need to place accountability without softening it.
You forgot a friend's birthday. You want to take the blame without excuses or explanation.
Someone asks whether a film counts as science fiction. It does, unambiguously, and you want to say so without qualifying.

distractors: Tangled into something so completely that you can no longer act or be understood alone.
A voluntary group of people doing the same kind of work who meet to trade what they learn.
Temporary structure that holds work up until the real thing can stand alone.
To make a bad situation worse.
Using far more words than the point needs.
